sources.title: Spain is the 2026 World Cup champion, defeating Argentina for its 2nd title
FIFA World Cup 2026 Final: Argentina vs Spain live updates
Spain GAME-WINNING Goal in 2026 FIFA World Cup™ Final 🏆Ferran Torres nets in Extra Time vs Argentina (video, FOX Sports)

chunks.text: On July 19, 2026, Spain {{pulled off}} [[one of the biggest]] wins in their history. At MetLife Stadium near New York, they {{took on}} Argentina in the [[final]] of the World Cup, the biggest event in soccer. After 90 minutes, no one had scored, so the game {{went on}} into [[extra time]]. [[At last]], Spain won 1-0 and {{picked up}} the World Cup [[trophy]] for the second time.

verbs.wrong: To score in the final minute
verbs.why: Underdogs pull off surprising wins, and thieves in movies pull off daring robberies. Spain pulled off a hard fought 1-0 win over Argentina to take the World Cup.

verbs.wrong: To beat a strong rival team
verbs.why: Boxers take on tough opponents, and underdog teams sometimes take on the biggest teams in a big game. In the final, Spain took on Argentina for the biggest prize in soccer.
A meeting can go on for hours, and an old family tradition can go on for generations. With no goals after 90 minutes, the World Cup final went on into extra time.

verbs.wrong: To pass the ball to a teammate
verbs.why: Winners pick up trophies after a big win, and shoppers pick up bags of groceries at the store. Spain picked up the World Cup trophy for the second time in their history.

chunks.text: For most of the match, Spain {{kept up}} the [[pressure]] and [[controlled]] the ball. Argentina's [[goalkeeper]], Emi Martinez, was [[superb]] and [[made save after save]]. Then, [[deep into]] extra time, the [[striker]] Ferran Torres {{broke through}}. In the 106th minute, he {{put away}} a shot from [[close range]], and Spain were [[in front]]. Martinez [[set a record]] with 11 [[saves]], but he could not {{keep out}} every shot.

verbs.correct: To keep something at the same level
verbs.wrong: To move the ball up the field fast
verbs.why: Runners keep up a steady pace, and workers keep up pressure to finish a project on time. For most of the match, Spain kept up the pressure and controlled the ball.

verbs.correct: To force a way past a defense
verbs.wrong: To kick the ball very hard
verbs.why: Sunlight breaks through storm clouds, and small startups sometimes break through in a crowded market. Deep into extra time, Spain's striker Ferran Torres finally broke through Argentina's defense.

verbs.correct: To score a goal in a game
verbs.wrong: To save a shot on goal
verbs.why: Strikers put away easy chances in the box, and top scorers put away shot after shot all season. In the 106th minute, Torres put away a close range shot to give Spain the lead.

verbs.correct: To stop something from getting in
verbs.wrong: To kick the ball far away
verbs.why: A good coat keeps out the cold, and a strong lock keeps out intruders. Argentina's goalkeeper made save after save, but he could not keep out every shot.

chunks.text: Argentina had [[dreamed of]] winning the World Cup two times [[in a row]]. Their star, Lionel Messi, is now 39, and this was [[almost certainly]] his last World Cup. But on this night, he could not {{take over}} the game the way he once did. Spain's young players never {{let up}}, and their [[defense]] stayed strong. Argentina tried to {{fight back}}, but they could not [[find a way through]].

verbs.why: A new manager can take over a struggling company, and a confident player can take over a match. At 39, Messi could not take over the game the way he once did.
Rain finally lets up after a long storm, and a hard worker's effort never lets up. Spain's young players never let up, and their defense stayed strong until the final whistle.
A sick person fights back after bad news from a doctor, and a losing team fights back in the second half. Argentina tried to fight back late in the game, but they could not find a way through.

chunks.text: When the final [[whistle]] went, the Spanish players fell to the ground in joy. For many fans, the win {{brought back}} happy memories of 2010, when Spain lifted their first World Cup. Sixteen years later, a new team has {{carried on}} that dream. Now Spanish soccer can {{look forward to}} [[a bright future]], with young stars [[leading the way]].

verbs.wrong: To call old players back to play
verbs.why: An old photo can bring back a childhood memory, and a song can bring back an entire summer. For many fans, the win brought back happy memories of Spain's first title in 2010.

verbs.wrong: To carry the cup through town
verbs.why: A family tradition can carry on for generations, and a good habit can carry on for years. Sixteen years after that first title, a new generation of players has carried on the dream.

verbs.correct: To feel happy about something coming
verbs.wrong: To get ready for the next final
verbs.why: Kids look forward to summer vacation, and workers look forward to the weekend. With young stars leading the way, Spanish soccer fans can look forward to a bright future.

mainIdea.s: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time to win the World Cup for the second time in their history. Their defense never let up, and Argentina's older star could not take over the match.
mainIdea.why: Spain won 1-0 in extra time, with a young striker scoring the only goal in the 106th minute. Their defense never let up, and Argentina's older star could not take over the game.

mainIdea.s: Spain scored early on a fast attack and held on for a narrow 1-0 win over Argentina in the final. Their tired defense let up near the end, but it was too late for Argentina to come back.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the winning goal came in the 106th minute of extra time, not early in the match. Spain's defense never let up until the very end.

mainIdea.s: Spain's national soccer coach said this year that he plans to step down once his current contract with the team ends. The federation said it would begin a search for a new coach soon after.
mainIdea.why: This is about the coach's future, not the final itself. The real story is Spain's 1-0 extra time win over Argentina in the World Cup final.

tf.s: Spain pulled off a 1-0 win over Argentina to take the World Cup.
tf.why: Spain pulled off a 1-0 win over Argentina in the final to win the World Cup for the second time.

tf.s: Ferran Torres put away the winning goal during extra time.
tf.why: In the 106th minute of extra time, Ferran Torres put away the shot that won the game.

tf.s: Argentina's goalkeeper kept out every single shot that Spain took.
tf.why: Emi Martinez made a record 11 saves, but he could not keep out every shot, and Spain scored.

tf.s: Lionel Messi took over the game and led Argentina to victory.
tf.why: Messi could not take over the game, and Argentina lost the final 1-0.

tf.s: For fans, the win brought back memories of Spain's first title in 2010.
tf.why: The win brought back happy memories of 2010, when Spain won their first World Cup.

tf.s: Spain's players let up in defense and stopped trying near the end.
tf.why: Spain's young players never let up, and their defense stayed strong.
